page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.large is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores using the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture running at 3.3 GHz. The processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1D cache. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, while network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 36.33 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving a top-tier result of 17.2 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4005.17 and a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 34.13 GB/sec. Memory performance is mixed, with a strong PassMark memory score of 2876.9, but a weak write bandwidth of 25.15 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, processing 6.51 million operations per second.

The m9gd.large offers a cost-efficient profile for general-purpose workloads that benefit from local NVMe storage and strong single-core execution. The primary tradeoff is the limited multi-core scaling and low baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It is well-suited for lightweight database operations, static web serving, single-threaded data compression tasks, and basic general-purpose application hosting. It is less suitable for multi-threaded high-performance computing or large-scale LLM inference due to poor multi-core and text generation benchmark results.
